headline: Extending HHJK (2019)'s frictions to 2023 and fitting a convergence law: the post-2010 talent-allocation slowdown is NOT a stall or reversal (WW continued (borderline, study-chosen cut-off), BM & BW slowed) but the exponential approach to a non-zero floor the model always implied; the remaining decline is tauH-dominated for BM/BW, while for WW tauW is ~half of it; and the projected forward friction 'dividend' is ~0.08%/decade of market GDP/person [PROJECTED, conditional on the fitted law, A, phi, z-tilde and q held at 2023 values], ~90x below the ~0.7%/yr of 1960-2010.

metrics.label: Stall classification (mean ln tau-hat): white women
metrics.note: 2010-23 decline = 34% of 1960-2010 rate; 2023 within law band b=0.19

metrics.label: Stall classification: Black men / Black women
metrics.note: neither stalled nor reversed; 2023 within own law's band (BM backtest tight e=0.010; BW wide e=0.125)

metrics.label: Post-2010 friction decline attributed to pre-market tauH
metrics.note: tauH-dominated for BM/BW with tauW flat; for WW tauW is ~47% of the decline (51% under R5). HRS (2024): the adjusted Black-white male wage gap stayed roughly flat even as measured discrimination fell. [corrected per 004 addendum]

metrics.label: Projected forward friction dividend (market GDP/person) [PROJECTED]
metrics.note: ~90x smaller; conditional on fitted law with A,phi,z,q held at 2023; NOT a growth forecast

metrics.label: Output permanently unrealised even at full convergence (tau->tau_inf)
metrics.value: ~8.8% [PROJECTED, conditional on the fitted law, A, phi, z-tilde and q held at 2023 values]
metrics.note: floors tau_inf ~1.28-1.60 are well above frictionless 1.0

tables.title: Convergence law per group (fit 1960-2010, true midpoints) + 2023 out-of-sample
Falling-tau contribution to market GDP/person: historical vs projected [PROJECTED]

figures.caption: Friction convergence law fit on 1960-2010 (solid = extrapolated law, dotted = fitted floor tau_inf) with the 2023 estimate as an out-of-sample test (diamonds, +/- band b). All 2023 points sit within the law's own band, so the post-2010 slowdown is the convergence the model implied, not a stall.
figures.alt: Three decaying curves (WW, BM, BW) for mean ln tau-hat from 1960 falling toward floors; 2023 diamonds near each curve with error bars.

figures.caption: Left: the 2010-2023 friction decline is tauH-dominated (pre-market), with tauW flat for BM/BW (for WW tauW is ~half the decline). Right: the projected forward friction dividend (~0.08%/decade [PROJECTED, conditional on the fitted law, A, phi, z-tilde and q held at 2023 values]; error band: WW backtest error 0.193 exceeds its projected decline 0.049) dwarfed by the ~6.9%/decade measured 1960-2010 historical contribution (and the measured 2010-23 contribution of ~0.06%/yr, ~8x the projection's annualized rate).
figures.alt: Left stacked bars of tauH vs tauW share of decline by group; right bars comparing 6.9% historical to 0.08/0.13/0.23% projected gains.

notes: No new data fetched; reuses 001 (living-update) 7-period friction estimates from saved .mat files. Items 1,2,4 are pure Python analysis; item 3 is 4 new Octave SolveForEqm solves per spec, stage-split (<=66s each), never backgrounded; a zero-shift run reproduces 001's 2023 baseline to the digit.

Pre-registered: law form, stall thresholds, band b=max(R1-R4 spread, backtest error), consistent 7-period inputs (B2), 1960-2000->2010 backtest (B1), [PROJECTED] labels (B3). WW/BW backtest errors are large (0.19/0.13) so their 'not stalled' verdict is low-power; BM's is confident.
All projection numbers are conditional illustrations of the fitted law (A, phi, z-tilde, q held at 2023), not a GDP growth forecast, and are not placed next to one.
